title: Creation of the world
summary: God speaks the world into being over six days, forming light, sky, land, sea, plants, sun, moon, animals, and finally man and woman in his own image, and calls the whole of it very good.

title: Adam, Eve, and Eden
summary: God rests on the seventh day, forms Adam from the dust, plants the garden of Eden for him to tend, and creates Eve as his companion from Adam's rib.

title: The fall in Eden
summary: The serpent tempts Eve to eat the forbidden fruit, she shares it with Adam, and God confronts the couple before expelling them from the garden of Eden.

title: Cain kills Abel
summary: Cain grows jealous when God favors Abel's offering over his own, murders his brother in the field, and is cursed to wander before Seth is born to replace Abel.

title: From Adam to Noah
summary: A genealogy traces the line from Adam through Seth down to Noah, recording long lifespans and noting that Enoch walked with God and was taken away without dying.

title: Noah builds the ark
summary: Seeing the earth's corruption and violence, God resolves to send a flood and instructs Noah to build an ark to save his family and pairs of every animal.

title: The flood begins
summary: Noah, his family, and the animals enter the ark as instructed, and God sends rain and rising waters that cover the earth and destroy all other life.

title: The floodwaters recede
summary: The floodwaters gradually recede, Noah sends out a raven and then doves to test for dry ground, and his family finally leaves the ark onto dry land.

title: God's covenant with Noah
summary: God blesses Noah's family, sets the rainbow as a sign of his covenant never to flood the earth again, and Noah's sons scatter after an incident involving his drunkenness.

title: The table of nations
summary: A genealogy lists the descendants of Noah's three sons spreading into the nations and languages of the earth, including the rise of the mighty warrior Nimrod.

title: The tower of Babel
summary: Humanity builds a city and tower to make a name for itself, God confuses their language and scatters them, and the line from Shem down to Abram is traced.

title: God calls Abram
summary: God calls Abram to leave his homeland for a land he will show him, promising to bless him and make him a great nation; Abram journeys to Canaan and later Egypt.

title: Abram and Lot separate
summary: Abram and Lot's growing herds cause conflict, so they part ways, with Lot choosing the fertile plain near Sodom while Abram remains in Canaan and receives God's promise again.

title: Abram rescues Lot
summary: A coalition of kings raids Sodom and captures Lot, so Abram leads a rescue, defeats the raiders, and is blessed by the mysterious priest-king Melchizedek.

title: God's covenant with Abram
summary: God reaffirms his promise of offspring and land to childless Abram, who believes him, and seals the covenant through a smoking pot and flaming torch passing between animal pieces.

title: Hagar and Ishmael
summary: Sarai gives her servant Hagar to Abram to bear a child, Hagar conceives and flees after conflict with Sarai, and an angel promises her son Ishmael many descendants.

title: The covenant of circumcision
summary: God renames Abram and Sarai as Abraham and Sarah, institutes circumcision as the sign of his covenant, and promises that Sarah herself will bear a son named Isaac.

title: Three visitors and Sodom
summary: Three visitors tell Abraham that Sarah will have a son within the year, and Abraham pleads with God to spare Sodom for the sake of any righteous people found there.

title: The destruction of Sodom
summary: Angels rescue Lot and his daughters from Sodom before God destroys the city, Lot's wife becomes a pillar of salt, and his daughters later bear sons through him.

title: Abraham and Abimelech
summary: Abraham again claims Sarah is his sister while staying with King Abimelech, who takes her but is warned by God in a dream and returns her unharmed.

title: Isaac is born
summary: Sarah gives birth to Isaac as God promised, Hagar and Ishmael are sent away into the wilderness, and Abraham makes a treaty with Abimelech at Beersheba.

title: Abraham offers Isaac
summary: God tests Abraham by commanding him to sacrifice Isaac, Abraham obeys until an angel stops him and provides a ram, and God renews his covenant promise.

title: Sarah dies
summary: Sarah dies in Hebron, and Abraham purchases the cave of Machpelah from the Hittites as a burial place for her and later for himself.

title: A wife for Isaac
summary: Abraham sends his servant to find a wife for Isaac among his relatives, and the servant's prayer is answered when Rebekah offers water to him and his camels.

title: Jacob buys Esau's birthright
summary: Rebekah gives birth to twins Esau and Jacob who struggle even in the womb, and the starving Esau later sells his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew.

title: Isaac and Abimelech
summary: Isaac repeats his father's deception about his wife while living among the Philistines, grows wealthy, and makes peace with Abimelech after disputes over wells.

title: Jacob steals the blessing
summary: With Rebekah's help, Jacob disguises himself as Esau to trick the aging, blind Isaac into giving him the blessing meant for his older brother.

title: Jacob's ladder at Bethel
summary: Fleeing his furious brother, Jacob dreams of a stairway to heaven at Bethel, where God repeats the covenant promises and Jacob vows loyalty to him.

title: Jacob serves Laban
summary: Jacob arrives at his uncle Laban's household, falls in love with Rachel, works seven years for her, but is tricked into marrying Leah first.

title: Jacob's children are born
summary: Through Leah, Rachel, and their servants, Jacob fathers eleven sons and a daughter, and he negotiates with Laban to build his own flocks before leaving.

title: Jacob flees from Laban
summary: Jacob secretly leaves Laban's household with his family and flocks, Rachel steals her father's household idols, and the two men make a covenant of peace at Gilead.

title: Jacob wrestles at Peniel
summary: Preparing to meet Esau, Jacob sends gifts ahead and wrestles all night with a mysterious man who renames him Israel before dawn.

title: Jacob reconciles with Esau
summary: Jacob fearfully approaches his brother Esau, who runs to greet him warmly, and the two reconcile before Jacob settles near Shechem.

title: The defilement of Dinah
summary: Jacob's daughter Dinah is assaulted by a local prince, and her brothers Simeon and Levi avenge her by deceiving and slaughtering the men of Shechem.

title: Jacob returns to Bethel
summary: Jacob returns to Bethel to worship God, is renamed Israel again, and Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin on the way to Ephrath.

title: Esau's descendants
summary: A genealogy records Esau's wives, sons, and descendants who become the nation of Edom, settling in the hill country of Seir.

title: Joseph is sold into slavery
summary: Joseph's dreams of ruling over his family provoke his brothers' hatred, and they sell him to traders who take him to Egypt as a slave.

title: Judah and Tamar
summary: Judah's daughter-in-law Tamar is denied a promised husband, so she disguises herself and tricks Judah into fathering her children to preserve the family line.

title: Joseph in Potiphar's house
summary: Joseph rises to oversee Potiphar's household but is falsely accused by Potiphar's wife after refusing her advances, and is thrown into prison.

title: Joseph interprets prison dreams
summary: In prison, Joseph correctly interprets the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker, but the cupbearer forgets Joseph once he is restored to his position.

title: Joseph rises to power
summary: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams of coming famine, is elevated to govern Egypt, and stores grain during seven years of plenty to prepare for the shortage.

title: Brothers come to Egypt
summary: Famine drives Joseph's brothers to Egypt for grain, where Joseph recognizes them but conceals his identity and tests them by keeping Simeon hostage.

title: The brothers return with Benjamin
summary: The brothers return to Egypt with Benjamin as required, and Joseph hosts them at a meal, seating them in birth order to their amazement.

title: Joseph tests his brothers
summary: Joseph plants his silver cup in Benjamin's sack and threatens to keep him as a slave, prompting Judah to offer himself in Benjamin's place.

title: Joseph reveals himself
summary: Overcome with emotion, Joseph reveals his identity to his stunned brothers, forgives them, and sends for his father Jacob to come live in Egypt.

title: Jacob moves to Egypt
summary: Jacob and his entire family travel to Egypt at Joseph's invitation, and Joseph tearfully reunites with his father after many years apart.

title: Israel settles in Goshen
summary: Joseph settles his family in the land of Goshen, presents them to Pharaoh, and manages Egypt's food supply during the ongoing famine.

title: Jacob blesses Joseph's sons
summary: Nearing death, Jacob adopts Joseph's two sons as his own and blesses them, crossing his hands to favor the younger over the older.

title: Jacob blesses his twelve sons
summary: Jacob gathers his twelve sons to pronounce blessings and prophecies over each of them before he dies and is prepared for burial.

title: Joseph forgives his brothers
summary: After Jacob's burial in Canaan, Joseph reassures his fearful brothers that God used their evil for good, and he dies in Egypt at the end of Genesis.
